Map a region of interest onto GLASS sinusoidal tiles

Source: R/find_tiles.R
glass_tiles_for_bbox.Rd

GLASS tiled products use the classic MODIS sinusoidal h/v grid (h<h>v<v> fragments in file names). These functions rebuild the exact tile polygons in the sinusoidal projection, transform them to WGS84 and intersect them with your region of interest, returning the tiles you need to download.

Usage

glass_tiles_for_bbox(lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max)

glass_tiles_for_sf(roi)

Arguments

lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max

WGS84 bounding box.

roi

A spatial vector object (sf/sfc, any CRS).

Value

An sf object (rows = tiles) with columns h, v, lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max, valid and the tile geometry in WGS84.

Examples

glass_tiles_for_bbox(120.8, 30.6, 122.2, 31.9)  # Shanghai
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 7 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 115.4701 ymin: 30 xmax: 143.5948 ymax: 40
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>    h v  lon_min  lon_max lat_min lat_max valid                       geometry
#> 1 28 5 115.4701 143.5948      30      40  TRUE POLYGON ((130.5407 40, 143....
